records.description_en: A rotation-axis control module in Luminos positioning systems for continuous or indexed rotational positioning.
An X-axis linear motion control module in Luminos positioning systems for precision lateral translation in optical alignment.
A Y-axis linear motion control module in Luminos positioning systems for precision lateral translation in optical alignment.
A yaw-axis control module in Luminos positioning systems for precise angular adjustment.
A Z-axis linear motion control module in Luminos positioning systems for precision axial positioning in optical setups.

The Luminos precision motorized positioning stage is a laboratory motion platform for precise positioning and optical alignment. It can include linear and rotary axes for adjusting the position and orientation of samples, probes, fibers, or optical components. The device supports homing, relative and absolute moves, and motion settings such as speed, acceleration, and microstep resolution, with both computer-controlled and manual knob operation.

The MC1 is a motor controller used to drive and position a linear actuator. It supports step increment control, travel limits, centering, reset, and point-to-point motion. In the lab, it is used for repeatable position scanning and adjustment, such as operating a linear actuator for Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) dip measurements.

The MC2000 is a motion controller for a motorized microscope stage or multi-axis translation stage, typically supporting X/Y/Z position readback, moves to target positions, and joystick-based manual control. In the lab it is used for precise sample positioning, scanning, and reproducible repositioning during microscopy.

The MDSnC is a multi-channel RF synthesizer used to drive an acousto-optic tunable filter (AOTF). It controls AOTF operation by supplying adjustable RF frequency and power to individual channels, and is commonly used for wavelength selection and light intensity control in spectroscopy, microscopy, and laser experiments.

The MP-285 is a 3-axis motorized positioning stage/micromanipulation system that provides precise motion in X, Y, and Z. It is commonly used in microscopy-based laboratory setups to position samples, probes, or optical components with micron-scale control and repeatability, with a controller for setting speed, resolution, and motion mode.

This is a continuous-wave laser made by MPB Communications, providing stable continuous laser output. In laboratories, it is commonly used for fluorescence excitation, optical alignment, microscopy, and other optical measurements that require adjustable laser power.

This is an automatic or semi-automatic wafer prober used for semiconductor wafer testing. It provides XY, Z, and rotational chuck positioning, contact/separation height control, vacuum holding, wafer map stepping, and optional thermal chuck capability. It is commonly used for wafer-level electrical measurements, device characterization, failure analysis, and test workflows with optional auto-loading, microscope, or silicon photonics alignment modules.

A laboratory peristaltic pump that moves liquid by compressing flexible tubing. It can run continuously or for a specified number of revolutions, and is commonly used for reagent transfer, recirculation, dispensing, and general fluid handling.

A laboratory peristaltic pump that can be controlled through serial communication for continuous pumping, timed dispensing, and batch liquid delivery. It supports control of start/stop, speed, direction, dispense mode, and run time, and can track volume and batch counts for reagent transfer, fluid-path control, and automated liquid handling.

A compact laser module used to provide stable optical excitation for fluorescence illumination, alignment, and general laser source needs in laboratory setups. It is commonly used in microscopy, optical experiments, and instrument integration.

A robotic system for controlling a Mecademic six-axis robotic arm and its end tools. It supports joint and Cartesian motion, gripper handling, vacuum pick-up, I/O control, program execution, and real-time monitoring for laboratory automation tasks such as pick-and-place, positioning, transfer, and sample handling.

A robotic arm control object for lab automation that can activate the robot, home it, disconnect it, and check IO module presence. It also manages dirty-state tracking for motion queue parameters and initialization settings so the robot can be restored to a known state before experiments or tests.

records.name_en: Mercury Stepper Motor Multi-Axis Motion Controller
records.description_en: This is a precision multi-axis motion controller for driving and controlling stepper-motor positioning stages. It is commonly used with motorized sample stages, microscope translation stages, or other linear/rotary axes. It supports position moves, position and motion-status readback, velocity setting, software travel limits, and joystick manual control, making it useful in microscopy, precision positioning, and laboratory automation setups.

This is a motion controller for precision positioning systems, used to control motorized stages or other motion assemblies in the lab via RS-232 serial communication. It supports motor enable/disable, homing, absolute and relative moves, position readback, and edge finding, and is commonly used for optical experiments, precision alignment, and automated positioning.

A compact laboratory syringe pump used to deliver liquids at a defined flow rate for precise, continuous infusion. It is commonly used for microfluidics, reagent addition, sample handling, and other experiments requiring accurate liquid dosing.

A piezo-driven Z-axis nano focusing stage for microscopes or precision positioning systems. It provides high-resolution vertical motion and fine focus control for microscopy, focus scanning, and precise sample positioning along the Z axis.

This is a precision microscope Z-axis nanopositioning stage for fine focusing and height positioning. It supports absolute and relative motion, zeroing, and position readback, and can report travel range and motion units. It is commonly used for focus scans, sample height adjustment, and autofocus-related microscopy experiments.

The NanoScan is a piezo-driven Z-axis nanopositioning stage or microscope focus stage used to precisely adjust the axial position of a sample or objective over micrometer-scale travel. It is commonly used for microscopy, autofocus, Z-scanning, surface profiling, and other experiments requiring fast and precise focus control.

records.name_en: New Scale MPM Micro Motion Controller
records.description_en: A motion-control interface for New Scale micro linear actuators/stages, supporting precision positioning and multi-axis control workflows.

This is a multi-axis motion controller for Newport Picomotor actuators. It can communicate over Ethernet or USB and supports RS-485 multi-controller networking. It is commonly used for high-resolution positioning and fine alignment in optical setups, precision positioning assemblies, and adjustment systems.

This is a laboratory multi-axis motion controller used to drive motorized translation or rotation stages. It is commonly used in microscopes, optical benches, and precision positioning setups to move and position samples, objectives, or optical components accurately.
The Newport ESP301 is an integrated 3-axis motion controller/driver for precision stages and actuators.

A multi-axis precision positioning stage driven by Newport Picomotor actuators, used for fine high-resolution adjustment of optical components, samples, or probes. It is commonly used in optical alignment, fiber coupling, microscopy, and other precision positioning tasks in the lab.

This is a networked precision motion controller used for laboratory positioning and motion applications. It drives and coordinates motorized stages and linear or rotary actuators, and is commonly used for optical alignment, sample positioning, scanning measurements, and automated experimental platforms. The controller can also store configuration, program, or log files for network-based file management.

Functional interface for a Newport XPS multi-axis motion controller over TCP/IP. It supports group initialization, homing, absolute and relative moves, trajectory execution, encoder and servo parameter configuration, GPIO triggering, event handling, and data gathering for precision stages and multi-axis positioning systems.
Newport XPS is a universal high-performance multi-axis motion control platform for complex trajectory and synchronized control tasks.
A serial communication driver for Next Generation syringe pumps, used in fluid infusion and programmable dispensing control.

A network-connected hub for Nobø electric heating systems. It can discover and connect heating zones and components on a local network, manage weekly schedules and comfort/eco/away overrides, and read zone or component temperatures for room heating and environmental temperature management in labs.

An OBIS laser is a laboratory laser light source commonly used for controlled illumination and excitation in microscopy and other optical experiments. It serves as a microscope light source, providing stable laser output with controllable on/off state and trigger behavior.

This is a motion controller for driving motorized positioning devices or stepper-motor axes. It can activate motors, configure motion-related parameters, move to a target position in counts, and report motion status and current position. It is commonly used in laboratories for precise positioning of optical components, sample stages, and linear or rotary translation assemblies.

A serial-controlled motorized translation stage, typically driven by stepper motors, for multi-axis positioning of samples or optical components. It supports relative/absolute motion, Z-axis focus scans, linear scans, and endstop-based homing, and is commonly used in microscopy, sample positioning, and repeatable scanning experiments.

This is a PCO Sensicam CCD camera for laboratory image acquisition. The driver indicates support for exposure control, trigger mode, region of interest (ROI), pixel binning, imaging mode configuration, and CCD image readout, making it suitable for scientific imaging and single or continuous acquisition tasks in the lab.

The PHD2000 is a laboratory syringe pump used to drive a syringe for precise liquid infusion or withdrawal. It is suited to experiments that require delivery of a defined liquid volume, such as sample delivery, fluid handling, and general laboratory dosing.

records.name_en: PI C-867 Two-Axis Piezo Positioning Stage
records.description_en: A PI C-867-based two-axis piezo/nanopositioning stage used for XY position readout, absolute and relative motion, velocity setting, servo control, and reference initialization. It is typically used for precision scanning, sample alignment, and nanometer-scale positioning in microscopy.

records.name_en: PI C-867 Dual-Axis Piezo Positioning Controller
records.description_en: This device is a motion controller for a dual-axis piezo positioning stage. It communicates over serial commands to enable servo control, perform referencing, set velocity, execute precise X/Y motion, and read back position, commonly for sample scanning and alignment in microscopy and other precision lab experiments.

A motion controller for piezo nanopositioners, supporting absolute/relative moves, servo enable control, position readback, and queries of control status and firmware information. It is commonly used for precision microscope focusing and high-resolution positioning experiments.

A motion controller for dual-channel or XY piezo positioning stages. It supports absolute/relative moves, closed-loop servo control, position readback, on-target checks, and reference initialization, commonly used for nanoscale positioning and scanning in microscopy.

A piezo positioning controller used to drive and read back a piezo actuator or piezo stage. It supports absolute moves, current position queries, and travel-range queries for microscopy, precision scanning, and focus positioning experiments.

A controller for precision positioning of a piezo stage or piezo actuator. It supports moving a channel to a target position, reading the current position, and querying control readiness, channel-related status, and motion limits. It is commonly used for microscope focusing and nanoscale positioning experiments.

A precision motion controller for driving a piezo positioning stage or piezo actuator. It communicates over a serial interface and supports position readback, absolute and relative moves, XY motion, on-target status checks, drift compensation, travel range queries, and firmware version retrieval. It is commonly used for microscope nanopositioning, focus control, and fine sample scanning.

This is an industrial PID process controller used in laboratory and equipment systems for closed-loop regulation of process variables such as temperature. It typically reads sensor feedback and drives heaters or other actuators to maintain stable control.

A simple PLC-controlled one-dimensional in/out motion device that travels between two mechanical limit positions. It is used to insert or retract a component from an experimental position or beam path, commonly for basic positioning, interlock demonstrations, and motion-control testing in beamline or laboratory setups.
A scientific detector camera entry in the PVCAM ecosystem, used for experimental image acquisition and camera parameter control.
A non-physical control component that sets positions and reads/writes status through process-variable interfaces, acting as an abstraction for higher-level motion control.
PhoxX is an OEM diode-laser series from Omicron-Laserage, offering controllable laser output and high-speed modulation for microscopy, fluorescence excitation, and optical instrumentation.

This is a motion controller for driving and controlling Picomotor micro-positioning actuators, typically connected to a computer via USB. It is commonly used in laboratories for fine optical alignment, small displacement adjustment of mounts or stages, and other applications requiring high-resolution mechanical positioning.

An illumination source used in a microscopy imaging system. The driver mainly provides on/off control and state query. The code notes that it pretends to be a laser only to reuse laser GUI controls, but the controlled object is better described as a switchable microscopy light source rather than a laser.

A motorized 2D translation stage for sample positioning on microscopes or laboratory platforms. It can report the current position, perform micron-scale relative motion in X and Y, move to specified coordinates, and check soft and hard travel limits to avoid overtravel.
A shutter used to control the illumination path of a Prior arc lamp. In microscopy and optical experiments, it is used to enable or block lamp light and to query the shutter state.

A temperature-control instrument used in laboratory workflows for setting temperature, reading back temperature, and checking device status. The interface also supports idle mode, version queries, debug output, and raw command execution for integration into automated experiments.

This is a motorized multiport valve used to switch fluid flow between multiple ports. In laboratories it is commonly used for flow-path selection, sample switching, and solvent routing in chromatography, flow analysis, and automated fluidic systems. The evidence indicates support for the Rheodyne MXII valve family and testing on the MXX778-605 10-port valve.

A two-finger electric robotic gripper used as an end effector, directly controlled over a network socket. It supports activation, open/closed state checks, automatic calibration of open and closed positions, and gripping motions with commanded position, speed, and force for sample handling and transfer in lab automation.

This is an electric three-finger adaptive robot gripper mounted on a robotic end effector. Its fingers can be controlled by position, speed, force, and grasping mode to handle objects of different shapes. It is commonly used in laboratory automation and robotic systems for grasping, transferring, and positioning samples, parts, or fixtures.

The DexArm is a desktop multifunction robotic arm that performs Cartesian motion and supports interchangeable end effectors such as a pen holder, laser engraving head, pneumatic picker, and soft gripper. It is used for education, laboratory automation, simple handling, drawing, laser processing, and small-scale automation tasks with accessories like conveyor belts and sliding rails.

A controller for Thorlabs SH05 and SH1 mechanical shutters. It manages shutter enable state, communication baud rate, operating mode, and timing, repeat, and trigger-related settings for beam blocking/unblocking and synchronization in optical experiments.

A SCARA robotic arm with a gripper for laboratory automation tasks such as positioning, transport, and pick-and-place operations. It can move in Cartesian space or joint space and perform homing, safe-position moves, and handling of plate-like lab consumables.

This is a motion controller for driving a stepper motor. It provides precise angular positioning with configurable direction and angle, and is suitable in laboratories for rotating sample mounts, optical components, or other mechanical parts.

A Timepix/Medipix pixel detector connected through the SPIDR readout system, used to configure the pixel matrix, DACs, test pulses, timing, and network readout parameters for data acquisition in particle, radiation, or fast imaging experiments.

An EPICS-controlled tri-sphere six-axis motion stage that supports individual or coordinated control of X, Y, Z translations and rX, rY, rZ rotations. It is used in laboratories for precise positioning and angular alignment of samples, optics, or fixtures.

This is a non-physical simulation component for the Hamilton STAR liquid handling platform. It provides mock machine configuration, tip status, 96-head firmware data, iSWAP status and positions, and simulated channel and iSWAP motion for development, debugging, command testing, and workflow validation rather than direct control of real hardware.

This is a non-physical software control component used as a background thread for the main Scientifica device class. It monitors position, initiates moves, tracks move status, handles stop and cancel requests, and reports position or objective changes via callbacks for coordinating and polling Scientifica motion devices.

records.name_en: Sensirion EK-H4 humidity and temperature sensor multiplexer box
records.description_en: A multiplexer box that connects over a serial port and reads up to four Sensirion humidity and temperature sensor channels. It is used in laboratory setups for multi-channel monitoring of temperature, relative humidity, and dew point.
